headline: Recommended that City Council create a letter of support for letting municipalities enforce building codes.
summary: The meeting covered updates on EV charging rates, plug-in solar, renewable diesel, and a renewable heating ordinance. Members discussed whether to recommend moving to 100% renewable energy but did not vote on it. Members voted unanimously to recommend a letter of support for municipal enforcement of building codes.
decisions: Recommended to City Council that it create a letter of support for allowing municipalities to enforce building codes, by unanimous vote.

decision_titles: Letter of support for municipal enforcement of building codes
plain_text:
South Burlington Energy Committee
September 23, 2026
The South Burlington Energy Committee held a regular meeting on Wednesday, September
23rd in Room 301, 180 Market St. and by Zoom remote participation.
Members present: Jean Sebastien Chaulot, Steve Crowley (Chair), Ethan Goldman, Fred
Kosnitsky, Carrie McLaughlin, MJ Reale (Vice-Chair)
Also present: Bettina Miguez (Climate Action Manager), Lou Bresee (Energy Project Manager -
online)
Member of the public: none
Welcome and Agenda review 
Comments and questions from the public not related to the agenda: none
Updates From Committee Members/Events and conferences attended:
    Gathering of Chittenden County energy committee people - no date set yet
    REV Conference 10/14
    Vermont Summit with Nate Hagen 9/29.  
    Ryan Hagen coming to the library next month - 10/17
Action - Fred to send MJ a blurb to pass along
Staff Reports
    Bettina - 
Attended VECAN plug in solar webinar 9/22.  There are no UL3700 certified systems yet. 
Biggest hurdle is still bi-directional GFCI wiring.  It is still not a plug-and-play system.  Three
experts presenting including Brattleboro person who did some organizing with community to
gauge interest and feasibility.  Law (7/1) says that HOAs cannot just say a blanket no, but can
develop "reasonable" requirements.
City submitting Charging Smart application by end of the month.  We are aiming for silver. 
When putting data together, noticed that only 351 households are signed up for GMP EV rates.
Brief discussion on awareness about rates. Might benefit from an educational push.
Learned at EAN meeting 500 MW of distributed solar in VT right now per GMP
    Lou
Meeting with gentlemen from Putney doing FLM work (flexible load management).  Reviewing
the way the building systems are controlled and looking for opportunities for FLM optimization
and energy efficiency in the City Hall building.
Renewable Diesel - organization leading that effort is Vermont Clean Communities (Peggy
O'Neil). Letter of intent approved by Leahy Institute.  The next step is for them to submit a
proposal for a pilot.  
Impact of Renewable Heating Ordinance - Ethan
    2023-2025 buildings have been built under this ordinance
41 single family, 21 multi-unit (50 units).  All had heat pumps.  No data on gas backups
    Expecting an estimated 90% reduction
    Results saw baseload go down indicating electric water heating is impactful
    Heating load did not change as much as expected with the hybrid gas/electric systems.
    Recommendations
Education 
Inspections
Modify Ordinance to encourage more electric heat usage
Extensive discussion on whether moving from 85% to 100% renewable source was something
the Energy Committee would want to recommend to City Council. Members were split on the
idea.
8:05 Enforcing Energy Code - Bettina
    Looking at residential building energy code compliance.  Working with a DOE grant -
realigning to make it about affordability.  Q:  Do municipalities have the authority to enforce
energy code?
    State-wide seeing less compliance with energy code in new construction (54%)
    State has not figured out how to execute and fund enforcement so the idea is to allow willing
municipalities to enforce
    Looking for letters of support from municipalities saying they would like to enforce
    Motion: Fred moves to recommend to city council that they create a letter of support for this
effort to allow municipalities to enforce building codes
    Ethan seconds
    Unanimous approval
Reflections on Green Community Event
    Good comments from the council in the city council meeting
    Natural Resources committee was happy
18 surveys, 5 emails
    Idea for 2027 - Special issue of the Other Paper or Insert in the Other paper with sections for
each committee
    Next year more signage about bus stop changes.
Action:  Carrie to reach out to Jonathan Dowds to see if he would come to committee to
discuss PUC
Action:  Talk to O'Brien about experience with space heating solely with heat pumps
Action:  Bettina to ask Zack to send slides from the EAN working group
The meeting was adjourned at 8:35 pm. Next meeting is October 28, 2026.
